preflight.missing-name: Add your name as the first line, starting with “# ”.
preflight.missing-email: No valid email address found. Add one under your name so recruiters can reach you.
preflight.missing-phone: No phone number found. Many recruiters still like to call.
preflight.invalid-email: “{value}” doesn't look like a valid email address.
preflight.invalid-url: “{value}” doesn't look like a working web address.
preflight.phone-format: Write “{value}” in international format, starting with + and the country code.
preflight.entry-date: “{title}” has no date an applicant tracking system can read. Put it in the third field: ### Title | Organisation | Date | Place.
preflight.entry-date.fix: Move the date to the date field
preflight.date-format-mixed: Your dates use more than one format ({styles}). Pick one and use it everywhere.
preflight.date-format-mixed.fix: Use the most common format everywhere
preflight.not-reverse-chronological: Entries in “{section}” aren't newest first. Most readers expect the latest role on top.
preflight.bullet-too-long: This bullet is {length} characters long. Try to keep bullets under {max}.
preflight.too-many-bullets: This entry has {count} bullets. {max} or fewer are easier to scan.
preflight.bullet-punctuation-mixed: Some bullets in this section end with a full stop and some don't.
preflight.invisible-characters: Your CV contains {count} invisible character(s), such as soft hyphens or zero-width spaces. They can break words for applicant tracking systems.
preflight.special-characters: Emoji and symbols ({chars}) may show up as boxes or be dropped by applicant tracking systems.
preflight.untitled-section: The section “{section}” has no visible heading, so applicant tracking systems can't tell what it is.
preflight.markup-diagnostic: Something in the formatting on this line couldn't be read.
preflight.nonstandard-heading: “{title}” isn't a common section heading. Standard headings like “Experience” or “Education” are easier for applicant tracking systems.
preflight.hidden-link-target: The link “{text}” hides its address ({href}). A printed CV or an applicant tracking system only sees the text.
preflight.photo-present: Your CV has a photo. In some countries (for example the US and UK) photos are discouraged.
preflight.custom-css: Custom CSS is active. Preflight can't check everything it changes.
preflight.margin-too-small: The {side} margin is {value} mm. Printers may cut off anything closer than {min} mm to the edge.
preflight.line-height-tight: Line spacing of {value} is tight and hard to read.
preflight.page-overflow: Something on page {page} doesn't fit and is cut off.
preflight.pages-over-target: Your CV runs to {pages} pages; the target is {target}.
preflight.sparse-last-page: The last page is only {fill}% full.
preflight.forced-split: An entry on page {page} was too tall to keep together, so it was split.
preflight.font-too-small: Some text is {size} pt. Keep it at {min} pt or larger so it stays readable.
preflight.low-contrast: Some text has a contrast ratio of {ratio}:1 against its background. Aim for at least {min}:1.
preflight.missing-font: The font “{family}” isn't loaded, so a fallback font is used instead.
preflight.multi-column: Your layout has more than one column with text. Applicant tracking systems read it in this order: {order}. For ATS-heavy applications, a one-column template is safer.
preflight.column-interrupts-entry: “{title}” continues on the next page, but applicant tracking systems read the other column before they get there.
diag.text-before-name: Text before your name is ignored. Start your CV with “# Your Name”.
diag.extra-name: Only the first “# ” line is your name. This one is shown as normal text.
diag.header-markup: Lists and entries don't work above the first section. Start a section with “## ” first.
diag.unclosed-emphasis: “{marker}” opens bold or italic text that is never closed.
diag.unsafe-link: The link “{url}” isn't allowed. Use http, https, mailto or tel links.
diag.entry-extra-fields: This entry has {count} fields separated by “|”; only 4 are used (title, organisation, date, place). Write \| for a literal bar.
diag.unparseable-date: “{date}” isn't a date format Recto understands, such as “Jan 2020 – Present” or “2019 – 2021”.
